name: application-tables
title: Tables
description: Semantic HTML table components for displaying structured data in dashboards and admin panels, with base, bordered, striped, sticky-heading, and sticky-column variants.
useWhen: Displaying structured relational data where rows and columns have a clear semantic relationship.
Users need to scan, compare, or sort multiple records across several attributes simultaneously.
An admin panel or dashboard needs a full data listing with row actions such as edit or delete.
avoidWhen: The data has only one or two columns — a simple list or definition list communicates this more cleanly.
The table would have more than eight or nine columns on desktop — consider hiding secondary columns or switching to a detail/master layout.
The primary use case is a summary of a single entity — a details-list or card is more appropriate.
responsiveBehavior: Tables scroll horizontally inside an overflow wrapper on small viewports. Sticky-column variants keep the first column fixed during horizontal scroll. Avoid hiding columns with display:none unless confirmed non-essential.
accessibility: Use <th scope='col'> for column headers and <th scope='row'> for row headers so screen readers announce the correct context.
Add a <caption> or aria-label to the <table> element to identify its purpose when the page has multiple tables.
Sortable column headers should use aria-sort='ascending' or 'descending' and be keyboard-focusable buttons.

variants.title: Base
variants.description: Clean table with a header row and alternating body rows, no borders — the standard starting point for data listings.
accessibility: Column headers use <th scope='col'>; all cells have sufficient color contrast against the white background.

variants.title: Base (Dark)
variants.description: Standard clean table adapted for dark dashboard surfaces with dark background header and body rows.
accessibility: Cell and header text must meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark table background.

variants.title: Bordered
variants.description: Table with visible borders on all cells, making column and row boundaries explicit — ideal for dense data or financial tables where precision matters.
accessibility: Borders provide visual structure; <th scope> attributes remain necessary for screen reader row/column association.

variants.title: Bordered (Dark)
variants.description: Bordered table adapted for dark surfaces, with visible cell borders distinguishable from the dark background.
accessibility: Border color must contrast with both the dark cell background and the cell text.

variants.title: Striped
variants.description: Table with alternating row background colors to improve row-tracking readability for wide tables with many columns.
accessibility: Stripe background colors are decorative; do not rely on stripe color alone to convey data meaning.

variants.title: Striped (Dark)
variants.description: Alternating-row striped table adapted for dark surfaces with subtle dark stripe differentiation.
accessibility: Stripe colors on dark backgrounds must still provide sufficient contrast for text within both row types.

variants.title: Sticky headings
variants.description: Table with a sticky header row that remains visible as the user scrolls vertically through a long data set — essential for tables with many rows.
accessibility: Sticky <thead> retains its semantics; ensure the sticky header background occludes scrolled rows fully to avoid visual confusion.

variants.title: Sticky headings (Dark)
variants.description: Sticky-header table adapted for dark surfaces, keeping the header visible against dark body rows during vertical scroll.
accessibility: Sticky header background must fully cover underlying dark rows to avoid readability issues at scroll boundary.

variants.title: Sticky first column
variants.description: Table with the first column fixed during horizontal scroll, allowing users to maintain row context when navigating many columns on narrow screens.
accessibility: Sticky column must have a solid background to prevent overlap with scrolling cells; use <th scope='row'> for identity columns.

variants.title: Sticky first column (Dark)
variants.description: Sticky-first-column table adapted for dark surfaces with the fixed column visually separated from scrolling columns.
accessibility: Sticky column background on dark theme must be opaque to prevent scrolling rows from bleeding through.
